---
title: "SACE and CSACE analysis using BART"
subtitle: "Treatment effects on outcomes truncated by death"
toc: false
---

When an outcome can only be measured on patients who survive — ventilator-free
days, length of stay, functional status — comparing arms among survivors
compares different sets of people, because survival is itself affected by
treatment. The **survivor average causal effect (SACE)** avoids this by defining
the effect among *always-survivors*: patients who would live under either arm.

This analysis estimates the SACE and the **conditional SACE (CSACE)** using
Bayesian Additive Regression Trees, then applies the same "fit-the-fit" idea used
in the [HTE pipeline](hte-pipeline.qmd) — a regression tree fitted to the
estimated conditional effects — to describe which patients the effect varies
across.

## Relation to the HTE pipeline

Both use BART to estimate a per-patient conditional effect and then fit a tree to
those estimates for interpretability. They differ in the estimand: the
[HTE pipeline](hte-pipeline.qmd) targets the conditional average treatment effect
on an outcome observed for everyone, while this analysis targets the effect among
always-survivors when the outcome is truncated by death.

Methodological background is in the
[publications](../publications.qmd), particularly Chen, Harhay, Tong and Li
(*Annals of Applied Statistics*, 2024) and Tong and colleagues (*Statistics in
Medicine*, 2025).
